tasks.goal: Evaluate best-practice Plaesy setup design from first principles. Neutral question: How should Plaesy initialize projects and onboard/configure users across technical and non-technical users, including a laptop without Plaesy installed, existing/new repos, task storage, and optional AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md integrations? Recommend commands, defaults, safety gates, and tradeoffs. Consider the current observed implementation: `plaesy tasks` searches upward for `.plaesy/` as project marker and stores ta

Skeptically assess failure modes and hidden costs in possible Plaesy init/onboard/config design for technical and non-technical users, including fresh laptops without CLI, existing repos/state, vault vs repo tasks, multiple repos/worktrees, agent instruction files, setup errors, upgrades, and no-network/offline paths. Recommend the safest product design. Current verified code: task CLI finds root by locating `.plaesy/` above cwd and stores tasks in `.plaesy/tasks/`; Memory settings vault is sepa

Pragmatically recommend how Plaesy should support project initialization and onboarding/configuration for ordinary non-technical and technical users. Simulate user journeys: no Plaesy on device, installed but no Memory setup, existing repo without .plaesy, pre-existing config/tasks, non-Git folder, team clone, offline/CI, agent integrations. State minimal high-value sequence, commands/UI, defaults, reversibility, and what to defer. Existing implementation: task root discovery requires `.plaesy/`

Research evidence relevant to product/CLI setup design for Plaesy: init versus onboarding/config, project-local versus user-local configuration, safe/idempotent init, non-technical user journeys, optional agent instruction file integrations. Inspect current Plaesy implementation if possible and use verifiable authoritative documentation for comparable tools (e.g. Cargo init, uv init, Docker Compose precedence, Git config).
